standard.title: Quelqu'un / Personne / Quelque chose / Rien (Indefinite Pronouns)
standard.explanation: French has four main indefinite pronouns: 'quelqu'un' (someone), 'personne' (no one), 'quelque chose' (something), and 'rien' (nothing). When 'personne' or 'rien' are used as the object of a verb, they require the negation word 'ne' before the verb. For example: 'Je ne vois personne' (I see no one), 'Il n'y a rien' (There is nothing). 'Quelqu'un' and 'quelque chose' are affirmative and do not require 'ne'. Example: 'Il y a quelqu'un à la porte' (Someone is at the door).

examples.english: I see someone at the window.

examples.french: Il y a quelque chose sur la table.
examples.english: There is something on the table.

advanced.title: Indefinite Pronouns — Quelqu'un, Personne, Quelque chose, Rien + Extended Uses
advanced.explanation: French indefinite pronouns distinguish affirmative and negative contexts. 'Quelqu'un' and 'quelque chose' are affirmative (someone, something) and never require 'ne'. 'Personne' and 'rien' are negative (no one, nothing) and always require 'ne' before the verb. Important distinction: 'personne' and 'rien' can also appear before the verb, in which case 'ne' is still required after them. Example: 'Rien ne change' (Nothing changes). Adjectives following 'quelque chose' or 'rien' use the preposition 'de' + masculine form: 'quelque chose de bon' (something good), 'rien de nouveau' (nothing new). Negative questions with 'personne' use the same structure: 'Y a-t-il quelqu'un?' (Is someone here?) vs. 'Il n'y a personne.' (There is no one).

standard.scenario: Introduce your extended family members to a friend. Mention at least three family members and describe what they do or where they live.
standard.modelAnswer: Je te présente mon oncle Marc et ma tante Sophie. Ils habitent à Lyon. Mon oncle travaille comme ingénieur. Ma cousine Anne habite avec nous. Elle va à l'école.
standard.modelAnswerExplanation: This answer correctly introduces family members using proper articles and prepositions, and provides additional information about where they live and what they do.
standard.tip: Use 'Je te présente' to introduce people. Remember to use the correct gender form: 'mon oncle' (my uncle), 'ma tante' (my aunt), 'mon cousin' (my male cousin), 'ma cousine' (my female cousin).

advanced.scenario: Describe your family structure in detail. Include both parents, siblings, and at least two extended family members. Explain relationships and where they live or work.
advanced.modelAnswer: Je t'explique ma famille. J'ai deux frères et une sœur. Mon père travaille en banque et ma mère est professeur. L'oncle de mon père habite à Marseille; c'est un médecin. La tante de ma mère vit avec nous. Elle a une fille, donc ma cousine Anne est née ici. Mon neveu, c'est le fils de ma sœur.
advanced.modelAnswerExplanation: This response uses detailed family relationships, includes locative information, and employs possessive structures like 'l'oncle de mon père' (my father's uncle). It distinguishes between family members living in different locations.
advanced.tip: Structure your response by first mentioning immediate family, then extended family. Use 'l'oncle de' (the uncle of) and 'la tante de' (the aunt of) for possessive relationships. Include professions and locations when relevant.
